title: Transactional Outbox

validation.research: Eight primary sources: Chris Richardson’s Transactional Outbox, Polling Publisher, and Transaction Log Tailing catalog entries; AWS Transactional Outbox; Particular Software’s NServiceBus Outbox; Debezium Outbox Event Router; SQLite Transactions; Python sqlite3. The established Transactional Outbox name and common Outbox Pattern shorthand are distinguished from an email outbox, transient queue, transactional inbox, receiving deduplication, and Event Sourcing. Broad exactly-once or cross-service atomicity claims are not inferred from product guidance. The article separates the local commit guarantee, later broker acceptance, and consumer completion, and makes relay liveness, ordering, stable identity, pending retention, and asynchronous failure ownership explicit.

runnable_example.verification: Exact demo output; original EUR 70.00 payload/schema/type/order version; atomic source commit; forced after-insert failure in either table rolls back both; duplicate order/event identity leaves no orphan; committed-only reads and same-connection active-transaction rejection; publisher executes without a held source transaction and permits another writer; empty/dispatched queues invoke no publisher; unavailable broker preserves pending intent; lost acknowledgment, dispatch-record failure after acknowledgment, and actual process death after durable acceptance all retry the same ID and bytes without repeating the order; source reopen and pre-commit crash recovery; original payload survives later business-state change; sequential single-worker pending delivery; exact total and ID boundaries; BEGIN/COMMIT errors roll back and permit retry; competing writers with one event identity leave one matching order/message pair. Durable acceptance log is a local test double, not a broker/consumer or a production ordering, authentication, parallel-relay, deduplication, or power-loss test.

example_limits: Original two-file Python 3.11+ standard-library SQLite simulation. One source transaction stores order O42 at 7000 euro cents and serialized OrderPlaced E901, schema one, order version one. A single-worker polling relay selects committed pending intent in sequence order, publishes without a held source transaction, and marks dispatched only after the publisher returns according to its acceptance contract. The publisher is a separately durable SQLite acceptance test log, not a network broker or consumer. Lost acknowledgment, mark failure after acknowledgment, and actual process death after log commit cause same-ID/same-payload retries; the order transaction is not repeated. Application data remains authoritative and outbox retention is separate from Event Sourcing. No production network broker, receiver deduplication, authentication, parallel relay claims, timeouts/backoff implementation, cleanup, broker partition/global ordering, or client retry protocol. Source BEGIN/COMMIT/insert failures, invalid boundaries, competing event identities, publisher outage, committed-only visibility, no transaction during publish, reopened files, and abrupt pre-commit recovery are tested; production power-loss and real messaging guarantees are not inferred.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, commit, push, or pull request.
